content.content:
You extract atomic propositions from a message as structured facts.
For each proposition output: subject, predicate (a listed predicate's shorthand, or a new short verb phrase), object, optional validFrom/validTo (ISO dates), a FactBank factuality value (CT+ certain-positive, PR+ probable-positive, PS+ possible-positive, and their - and CTu/Uu variants), polarity (+/-/?), optional confidence 0..1, optional nature (epistemic/aleatory), the speech act as force (assertive|directive|commissive|expressive) and mood (declarative|interrogative|imperative), the source quote, optional subjectType/objectType (person|org|place|event|concept|thing), graph (a short name for the group of propositions it belongs to), and predicateDescription (only for a new predicate).
Rules:
1. Capture uncertainty in factuality ("probably" => PR+, "might" => PS+).
2. Keep prepositions and particles that bind to the verb in the predicate, not the object: passive voice "X was created by Y" => predicate "created by", object "Y" (just the agent). Likewise "moved to", "depends on", "reported by".
3. Use the predicate "is_a" for class membership: "Socrates is a man" => subject "Socrates", predicate "is_a", object "man". A job title or role is "has_role" instead: "Rich is the founder" => subject "Rich", predicate "has_role", object "founder". Never use bare "is" or "was".
4. Give propositions from the same sentence the same graph name, and propositions from another sentence a different one.
5. Keep every predicate in timeless present form and express tense through validFrom/validTo instead: "Alice worked at Acme until 2020" => predicate "works at" with validTo set from the stated end. Past tense alone — without an explicit date or an end cue such as "until", "former", or "no longer" — does NOT set validTo.
6. Prefer short, reusable predicates and reuse the SAME predicate for the same relation throughout ("works for" / "employed by" => the listed "works_for"). Never invent a synonym variant of a listed predicate or of one you have already emitted.
7. The object must be a single concrete entity (a person, project, org, place, or thing) or a literal value — never a raw id, snowflake, URL, or channel reference. Drop the proposition if the only object would be such an opaque token.
8. Emit a proposition only when BOTH its subject and object are concrete and named. If either would be an unresolved pronoun (we/it/they/this/that) or otherwise unknown, omit the proposition entirely — never output "unknown" as a subject or object.
9. Classify each proposition by speech act. A statement the author commits to => force "assertive", mood "declarative" (this is the default — omit force to mean assertive). A request that the recipient do something => force "directive", mood "imperative", factuality "Uu": subject = who is asked to act, predicate = the requested action, object = the thing. A question the author asks => force "directive", mood "interrogative", factuality "Uu": the proposition being asked about. The author's own promise/offer => force "commissive". Requests and questions are still subject to the previous rule: emit them ONLY when both subject and object are concrete and named.

Predicates. Use the shorthand of the one that fits the relation (or any of its forms). Only when none fits, write a new short verb phrase in timeless present form and set predicateDescription to one sentence saying what it relates:
- is_a: "is a" (also: is an, is instance of) — A class the subject is an instance of: "Socrates is a man".
- kind_of: "kind of" (also: is kind of, is type of, is a type of, subclass of) — A broader class every instance of the subject class belongs to: "a philosopher is a kind of thinker".
- same_as: "same as" (also: also known as, aka, is the same as) — The subject and object are one and the same entity.
- has_role: "has role" (also: works as, is on the team as, role, job title) [person → any] — The role or job title the subject holds.
- member_of: "member of" (also: belongs to, is member of, is on the team, is on team) [person → organization] — The organization or team the subject belongs to.
- has_member: "has member" [organization → person] — A member of the organization or team.
- works_for: "works for" (also: works at, employed by, is employed at) [person → organization] — The organization that employs the subject.
- founded: "founded" (also: is founder of, established, started) [person → organization] — An organization the subject founded; schema.org states it the other way round (`schema:founder`).
- alumni_of: "alumni of" (also: studied at, graduated from) [person → organization] — A school or organization (never a person) the subject studied at or was formerly part of.
- knows_about: "knows about" (also: is expert in, is the one to ask about, expert in, specializes in) — An area the subject can answer questions about.
- located_in: "located in" (also: lives in, is based in, based in, is located in) [any → place] — Where the subject is.
- born_in: "born in" (also: was born in, birthplace) [person → place] — The place the subject was born.
- about: "about" (also: is about, concerns, covers) — The topic a document, message or event is about.
- mentions: "mentions" (also: refers to, cites) — An entity a document or message mentions without being about it.
- text: "has text" (also: wording) — The wording of a message, question or document.
- knows: "knows" (also: is friends with, is acquainted with, met) [person → person] — A person the subject knows.
- has_account: "has account" (also: is on discord as, username, handle) — An account the subject uses, such as a Discord username.
- created_by: "created by" (also: authored by, written by, made by) [any → person] — Who made the subject (a document, a project, a thing).
- part_of: "part of" (also: is part of, component of) — A larger whole the subject is part of.
- depends_on: "depends on" (also: requires, needs) — Something the subject cannot work or happen without.
- related_to: "related to" (also: is related to, is associated with) — An associative link when no more specific predicate fits.
- claim: "claim" — A remembered statement about the subject, in the agent’s words.
- has_note: "has note" — Notes about the subject, in markdown.
- helps_with: "helps with" (also: will help with, helping with) — Work the subject helps with.
- works_on: "works on" (also: working on, will work on) — A project or task the subject is working on.
- uses: "uses" (also: is using, built with, adopted, switched to, relies on) — A library, tool, language or service the subject uses (a person, a project or a codebase).
- completed: "completed" (also: finished, done) — A task the subject finished.
- shipped: "shipped" (also: ships, released) — Something the subject released.
- proposes: "proposes" (also: suggests) — An idea or change the subject put forward.
- asked: "asked" (also: asks, asked question) — A question the subject asked: a node typed schema:Question whose `has text` is its wording.
- received: "received" — Something the subject was sent.
- archived: "archived" — Something the subject archived.
- deleted: "deleted" — Something the subject deleted.
- filed: "filed" — Something the subject filed (an issue, a report).
- drafted: "drafted" — Something the subject drafted.
- notified: "notified" — Someone the subject notified.
- relayed: "relayed" — A message the subject passed on.
- awaiting: "awaiting" (also: waiting for) — Something the subject is waiting for.

Known entities. When a subject or object refers to one of these, spell it exactly as listed:
- Bob (person)
- Bob (person)

Author: unknown
Date: unknown
Message:
[2026-11-19T21:36:55.287Z] Bob: FYI: we decided to ship offline mode this quarter, and I'm working on background sync.

response.text:
I'm pulling the claims out of Bob's message. The first sentence has an unclear "we," so I'll leave that one out. In the second, Bob says he is working on background sync.

I'm checking which claims are concrete enough to include. "Background sync" is a named task, and Bob is the author, so he can serve as the subject. The "offline mode" sentence has an unresolved "we," so I'll leave it out.

```json
[
  {
    "subject": "Bob",
    "subjectType": "person",
    "predicate": "works on",
    "object": "background sync",
    "objectType": "thing",
    "factuality": "CT+",
    "polarity": "+",
    "force": "assertive",
    "mood": "declarative",
    "source": "I'm working on background sync.",
    "graph": "msg-2026-11-19T21:36:55Z"
  }
]
```

The first sentence ("we decided to ship offline mode this quarter") yields no proposition because its subject, "we," is an unresolved pronoun.
